artifacts.summary: 5-phase plan landing both remedies for the plan-revision/implement race: one new context/patterns contract file, an unconditional sentinel-write clause in the plan-revision aux prompt, a static (hash-safe) staleness pointer in the implement dispatch block, a narrow pre-write re-read obligation in both implementation agents, and a final byte-budget/redeploy/full-gate phase.

memory_candidates.content: When adding any new line to a composed /orchestrate dispatch file (orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh or an aux counterpart), check first whether the value varies per cycle. orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's cycle_plan_dispatch_hash() normalizes a dispatch file by stripping exactly three known per-cycle-varying lines before hashing it, and the IDENTICAL DISPATCH HALT compares those hashes across cycles. A new varying line that is not added to that strip pattern in the SAME change silently renders the halt inert (this already happened once, between 2026-10-03 and a later repair, and is pinned by test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's Group 27 Case F). The architectural consequence generalizes: freshness or staleness signals about a file an agent will read belong to the agent's own first read, not to dispatch-build time, because the race window is between the agent's read and its write. Emitting a build-time mtime or hash both breaks the halt and measures the wrong interval.
